name: Primitive-First Plasma Physics

phase_0.boundary_condition: The collective dielectric response within the self-consistent electromagnetic field

VINIT.justification: The neutral state before the separation of charge defines the uninitialized manifold.

TANCH.justification: The characteristic scale beyond which electric fields are screened, providing the system boundary.

AFWD.justification: The forward transformation from neutral atoms to the ionized plasma state.

AREV.justification: The reverse transformation where ions and electrons regain neutral stability.

CLINK.justification: The coupling of particle distribution functions to the self-consistent field evolution.

IMSCRIB.justification: The fundamental self-referential oscillation of electrons responding to their own displacement.

FSPLIT.justification: A neutral volume splitting into distinct electron and ion populations.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of a neutral collective fluid from the electron and ion branches.

EVALT.justification: The state where individual particle motions successfully correlate into waves.

EVALF.justification: The failure of the wave state as energy is absorbed back into individual particle velocities.

ENGAGR.justification: A paradice state where the boundary is simultaneously a vacuum potential and a particle flux.

IFIX.justification: The permanent fixation of magnetic flux lines within the high-conductivity fluid element.

phase_3.void_description: Neutral gas with zero collective electromagnetic interaction
phase_3.true_description: Sustained MHD wave oscillation with positive phase velocity
phase_3.false_description: Thermal decay and loss of collective containment
phase_3.both_description: Wave-particle resonance: energy held in both the field and the velocity distribution

steps.domain_action: Neutral atomic gas occupies the vacuum manifold
External energy injection initiates the ionization morphism
Electrons recognize the local electric field and establish the plasma frequency
Local thermal fluctuations split the fluid into electron and ion charge branches
The electron branch supports high-frequency Langmuir oscillations
Recombination descent occurs on the ion branch as cooling begins
Ion-acoustic damping on the reverse branch attempts to destabilize the fluid
Quasineutrality reintegrates the charge branches into a long-range collective unit
The unit couples to the magnetic field via the Alfvén velocity
The magnetic field lines are permanently fixed into the plasma trajectory
The Debye sheath holds the non-neutral boundary potential in equilibrium with the bulk
The system reaches terminal anchors at the boundary of the containment vessel

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Coulomb collision operator translating velocity vectors into thermal distributions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Particle distribution function in six-dimensional phase space
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The characteristic plasma timescales (electron vs ion plasma periods)

phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle is governed by reversible Hamiltonian dynamics in the collisionless limit
